mainTopic: The rules of עיבור השנה: רבן גמליאל's letters, the reasons for adding a month, and where and when it must be declared
overview: The amud opens by finishing a comparison between the stern earlier leaders and the humble later ones. It then brings a ברייתא about three letters רבן גמליאל dictated: two announce ביעור מעשרות, and one tells the גולה that he added thirty days to the year. That letter mentions 'my colleagues', but the גמרא suggests it was written after he was removed from office. Next, a ברייתא lists three reasons for עיבור השנה (unripe grain, unripe tree fruit, and the תקופה) and requires two of them. A question about what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל meant ends in תיקו. Another ברייתא checks three regions of the land and gives יהודה special weight, because the עומר comes from there. The גמרא then rules that עיבור should be done in יהודה, with חנניה איש אונו holding that it does not count in the גליל at all. It also rules that leap years and new months are declared only by day, proven from a פסוק calling it a משפט. A new ברייתא about when a leap year is not declared begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Stern earlier leaders versus humble later leaders
steps.stepSummary: The end of a statement comparing the earlier, stern leaders with the later, humble ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: [See the difference between] the earlier, stern leaders and the later, humble leaders.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a sentence that began earlier: it is pointing out a contrast between the stern leaders of an earlier generation and the humble leaders who came later. It is also setting up the ברייתא that comes next, which shows the earlier style.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The surprise is that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, known for humility, wrote his announcement in a less modest way than his father רבן גמליאל, known for being stern. The next step quotes רבן גמליאל's letters so we can compare the two styles.

keyTerms.meaning: Stern, forceful people (here: leaders known for strictness)
The earlier ones
Humble people
The later ones

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of a sentence that started before this section. Do not read it as a new topic. It is the conclusion of a comparison, and the ברייתא that follows is the evidence for it.

phrases.english: the earlier, stern ones
and the later, humble ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a comparison begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a noticeable difference in style between the earlier stern leaders and the later humble leaders.

steps.title: The scene: רבן גמליאל on the הר הבית with his scribe
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא opens a story: רבן גמליאל sits on a step on the Temple Mount, his scribe stands in front of him, and three blank letters are ready.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: Once רבן גמליאל was sitting on a step on the הר הבית. יוחנן, that scribe, was standing in front of him, with three cut sheets for letters laid out before him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as its source. This step only sets the scene; the content of the letters comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word דתניא ('as it was taught') shows that this story is the proof for the comparison in step 1. The three prepared sheets tell us right away that three separate letters are about to be dictated.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a story
The Temple Mount
Letters, documents

phrases.english: As it is taught: There was an incident with Rabban Gamliel

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה יוֹשֵׁב עַל גַּב מַעֲלָה בְּהַר הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: who was sitting on a step on the Temple Mount,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיָה יוֹחָנָן סוֹפֵר הַלָּז עוֹמֵד לְפָנָיו,
phrases.english: and Yochanan, that scribe, was standing before him,
and three cut documents were placed before him.
phrases.notes: These are blank sheets of parchment, already cut to size and ready to write on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that supports the comparison in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The comparison of the stern earlier leaders' style
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about רבן גמליאל's letters

steps.title: Letters to the גליל and the דרום about ביעור מעשרות
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל dictates two letters: one to the upper and lower גליל about separating מעשר from olives, and one to the דרום about separating מעשר from grain, because the time for ביעור has arrived.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to the scribe: Take one letter and write: 'To our brothers, the people of the upper גליל and the lower גליל, may your peace grow. We are letting you know that the time of ביעור has come, to separate מעשר from the vat of olives.' And take another letter and write: 'To our brothers, the people of the דרום, may your peace grow. We are letting you know that the time of ביעור has come, to separate מעשר from the piles of grain stalks.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the wording of the first two letters. Both tell people that the time for ביעור מעשרות has come and that they must separate the tithes they still owe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each region gets the produce that is typical there: olives in the גליל and grain in the דרום. These two letters are routine announcements. The wording that matters for the comparison in step 1 comes in the third letter.

keyTerms.meaning: ביעור: the required clearing out of tithes not yet given away
The tithe (מעשר)
To separate (set aside)
The vat where olives are stored before pressing
Piles (sheaves) of grain stalks

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: טוֹל אִיגַּרְתָּא חֲדָא וּכְתוֹב:
phrases.english: He said to him: Take one document and write:
To our brothers, the people of the Upper Galilee,
and to our brothers, the people of the Lower Galilee,
may your peace increase.
We are informing you
that the time of eradication has arrived,
phrases.notes: This is the time when any tithes you still have at home must be given out or removed.

phrases.english: to separate the tithe from the vat of olives.
And take one document and write:
To our brothers, the people of the South, may your peace increase.
We are informing you
that the time of eradication has arrived,
to separate the tithe from the mounds of grain stalks.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: טוֹל אִיגַּרְתָּא חֲדָא וּכְתוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the text of the first two letters.
steps.raayaObject: The style in which רבן גמליאל announced decisions
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of the first two letters in the ברייתא

steps.title: Letter to the גולה: thirty days added to the year
steps.stepSummary: The third letter tells the Jews of בבל, מדי and all the גולה that, because the young birds and lambs are not ready and spring has not come, he and his colleagues decided to add thirty days to the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: And take one letter and write: 'To our brothers in the גולה of בבל, our brothers in מדי, and all the rest of the גולה of ישראל, may your peace grow forever. We are letting you know that the young birds are still tender, the lambs are still thin, and the time of spring has not arrived. The matter seemed good to me and to my colleagues, and I have added thirty days to this year.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the third letter, which announces עיבור השנה, adding a month to the year. The key words are 'good to me and to my colleagues', which seem to show רבן גמליאל including others in the decision.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasons are practical. Young birds and lambs for קרבנות are not ready yet, and spring (needed for פסח) has not come. The phrase 'my colleagues' suggests that the נשיא made the decision together with others, and the next step questions that inference.

keyTerms.meaning: The Diaspora (גלות)
Young birds, fledglings
Lambs
Spring (the season of אביב)
My colleagues
And I have added

steps.whyThisMatters: This letter is the main source that עיבור השנה was announced by the נשיא, and it raises the question of whether he acted alone or together with colleagues.

phrases.english: And take one document and write:
To our brothers, the people of the Diaspora in Babylonia,
and to our brothers who are in Media,
and to the rest of the entire Diaspora of Israel,
may your peace increase forever.
We are informing you
that the fledglings are tender,
and the lambs are thin,
and the time of spring has not arrived,
and the matter is good before me and before my colleagues,

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹסֵיפִית עַל שַׁתָּא דָּא יוֹמִין תְּלָתִין.
phrases.english: and I have added thirty days to this year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא with the third letter, which holds the key phrase about colleagues.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן גמליאל included his colleagues in the decision to add a month to the year
steps.raayaSupportSource: The phrase 'before me and before my colleagues' in the third letter

steps.title: Perhaps this was after he was removed from office
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference: perhaps this letter was written after רבן גמליאל was removed as נשיא, when he shared the leadership with others.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps this happened after they removed him from office.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea that the third letter proves רבן גמליאל normally included his colleagues. It suggests this letter may come from a later period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל was removed as נשיא for a time, and after he returned he shared the position with others. If the letter was written then, mentioning colleagues reflects that special situation, not his normal practice. So the letter cannot prove how he acted earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, maybe (used to push back on a proof)
After
That they removed him (from his position)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's letter mentions 'my colleagues', but the גמרא blocks the proof: that letter may come from after רבן גמליאל's removal from office, when he no longer led alone.
steps.confusionAlert: The word עברוהו here means 'they removed him from office.' It is not about עיבור השנה, even though the two words look alike.

phrases.english: Perhaps it was after they deposed him.
phrases.notes: He means after רבן גמליאל was removed as נשיא. When he returned, he shared the role, so he wrote 'my colleagues'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn from the third letter's mention of colleagues.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the 'colleagues' wording as evidence of רבן גמליאל's normal practice
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The letter may date from after his removal from office, when he shared leadership, so it does not show how he acted when leading alone.

steps.title: Three reasons to add a month to the year
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three signs that can justify making the year a leap year: unripe grain, unripe tree fruit, and the season. Two signs are needed; one alone is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: There are three reasons to add a month to the year: the grain is not ripe yet, the fruit of the trees is not ripe yet, and the season (the calendar's sun cycle). If two of these apply, they add a month. If only one applies, they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that lists the three reasons a בית דין may add a month to the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a rule about when עיבור is allowed. One sign alone is too weak a reason. Two signs together are enough. The next part of this ברייתא adds which of these signs makes everyone happy.

keyTerms.meaning: They make the year a leap year by adding a month (a second אדר)
Ripening of the grain (barley) in spring
Fruit of the trees
Season, the sun-based point in the year (equinox)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה –
phrases.english: For three things they add a month to the year:
for the ripening of the grain,
phrases.notes: Meaning: when the barley is not ripe yet.

phrases.english: and for the fruit of the trees, and for the season.
For two of them, they add a month,
but for one of them, they do not add a month.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the reasons for עיבור, after the discussion of רבן גמליאל's letter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A year is made a leap year only when at least two of the three signs (grain, tree fruit, season) apply.

steps.title: When grain is one of the reasons, everyone is happy
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that people are happy when unripe grain is one of the reasons. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: 'For the season.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And when the unripe grain is one of the two reasons, everyone is happy. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: for the season.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and says which kind of leap year makes people happy. Then רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds a short comment that is not clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the grain is still unripe, nobody loses by waiting an extra month for ניסן. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only says 'for the season,' and it is not clear what he is adding. That unclear wording sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone is happy

phrases.english: And when the grain ripening is one of them,
everyone is happy.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: עַל הַתְּקוּפָה.
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: for the season.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁאָבִיב אֶחָד מֵהֶן הַכֹּל שְׂמֵחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with an added detail and a תנא's comment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A leap year based partly on unripe grain pleases everyone. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds 'for the season,' but his meaning is unclear.

steps.title: What did רבן שמעון בן גמליאל mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל meant that people are happy because of the season, or that the season alone is enough to add a month.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Did he mean that people are happy when the season is the reason? Or did he mean that they add a month for the season alone?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about which part of the ברייתא רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was commenting on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to read him. First: he is talking about the 'everyone is happy' line, and the season is what makes people happy. Second: he is talking about the 'two reasons' rule, and the season alone is enough for עיבור. The second reading would change the actual rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them

phrases.english: A question was asked among them:
Is it over the season that they are happy,
or is it for the season alone that they add a month?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's short comment in step 7 refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'על התקופה' refers to the happiness clause or to the rule of עיבור itself.

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves the question unresolved: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: It stands (the question is not answered).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it cannot settle the question, so it leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source decides which reading is right. Both meanings of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל stay possible.

keyTerms.meaning: The question stands unresolved

phrases.english: It stands unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 8 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We do not know whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was talking about the happiness clause or the rule itself.

steps.title: Three regions are checked, and יהודה matters most
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says the בית דין looks at three regions: יהודה, עבר הירדן, and the גליל. If two need more time, they add a month, but not for one. When יהודה is one of the two, everyone is happy, because the עומר comes only from יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: They add a month to the year based on three regions: יהודה, עבר הירדן, and the גליל. If two of them need it, they add a month. If only one does, they do not. When יהודה is one of them, everyone is happy, because the עומר is brought only from יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא with the same 'two out of three' pattern, this time about regions of the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule works like the one in step 6: one region alone is not enough, but two are. יהודה is special because the עומר is brought from there. Its crops need to be ready by ניסן, so a leap year that helps יהודה pleases everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: The southern region of ארץ ישראל, around ירושלים
The land east of the Jordan river
The northern region of ארץ ישראל
The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה אֲרָצוֹת מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה –
phrases.english: Based on three regions, they add a month to the year:
Judea, Transjordan, and the Galilee.
For two of them, they add a month,
but for one of them, they do not add a month.

phrases.aramaic: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁיְּהוּדָה אַחַת מֵהֶן – הַכֹּל שְׂמֵחִין,
phrases.english: And when Judea is one of them, everyone is happy,
because the omer comes only from Judea.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה אֲרָצוֹת מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ברייתא that applies the same 'two out of three' rule to regions instead of signs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עיבור requires a need in two of the three regions. A need in יהודה is the most welcome, since the עומר comes from there.
steps.whatToRemember: Both lists work the same way: two out of three is enough, one is not. In each list, one item (אביב, יהודה) makes everyone happy.

steps.title: עיבור should be done only in יהודה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that the בית דין makes the year a leap year only while sitting in יהודה. Still, if they did it in the גליל, it counts after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: They make leap years only in יהודה. But if they made it a leap year in the גליל, it is still a leap year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about where the בית דין must be located when it adds a month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up two levels. To start with, the בית דין should only do it in יהודה. After the fact, a leap year declared in the גליל is still valid.

keyTerms.meaning: They made it (the year) a leap year
It is a leap year (valid)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנִים אֶלָּא בִּיהוּדָה,
phrases.english: They add a month to the years only in Judea,
but if they made it a leap year in the Galilee, it is a leap year.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנִים אֶלָּא בִּיהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reasons for עיבור to the place where it must be done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ideally עיבור is done only in יהודה, but if done in the גליל it is valid after the fact.

steps.title: חנניה איש אונו: in the גליל it does not count
steps.stepSummary: חנניה איש אונו testifies that a leap year declared in the גליל is not valid, even after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: חנניה איש אונו testified: If they made it a leap year in the גליל, it is not a leap year.
steps.whatsHappening: An opposing opinion is brought. חנניה איש אונו disagrees with the end of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said 'only in יהודה' is the ideal, but a leap year made in the גליל still works. חנניה איש אונו says 'only in יהודה' is required: a leap year made in the גליל is not valid at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He testified (passed on a ruling he received)
It is not a leap year

phrases.english: Chananya of Ono testified:
If they made it a leap year in the Galilee, it is not a leap year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the second half of the ברייתא in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A leap year declared in the גליל is not valid at all.

steps.title: What is the reason of חנניה איש אונו?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי asks what source supports חנניה איש אונו's strict view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה, son of רבי שמעון בן פזי, said: What is the reason of חנניה איש אונו?
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא asks for the source behind חנניה איש אונו's opinion. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying that a leap year done in the wrong place does not count at all is a strong claim. A strong claim like that needs a source, so the גמרא looks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
The son of

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, said:
What is the reason of Chananya of Ono?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the source of the opinion in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for invalidating a leap year declared outside יהודה.

steps.title: The פסוק: every ruling must come from near the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: The answer is a פסוק, 'לשכנו תדרשו ובאת שמה.' It teaches that every ruling you work out must be made in the dwelling place of the מקום, which means יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'To His dwelling you shall seek, and you shall come there.' This teaches that every ruling you work out must be made only near the dwelling place of the מקום.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers his own question with a פסוק that ties legal rulings to the place of the שכינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תדרשו ('seek') is read as 'working out rulings.' לשכנו ('His dwelling') points to the area near ירושלים. So a ruling like עיבור made far away in the גליל does not count, which supports חנניה איש אונו.

keyTerms.meaning: To His dwelling you shall seek
Rulings or inquiries that you work out
A name for הקב״ה (the Omnipresent)

phrases.english: The verse says: 'To His dwelling you shall seek, and you shall come there,'
all the rulings that you work out

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִהְיוּ אֶלָּא בְּשִׁכְנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם.
phrases.english: must be only in the dwelling place of the Omnipresent.
phrases.notes: In practice this means the area of יהודה, close to ירושלים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: לְשִׁכְנוֹ תִדְרְשׁוּ וּבָאתָ שָּׁמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'לשכנו תדרשו' requires every legal ruling to be made near the dwelling of the שכינה, so עיבור in the גליל is not valid.
steps.whatToRemember: The first opinion: 'only in יהודה' is the ideal, but עיבור in the גליל still works after the fact. חנניה איש אונו: עיבור in the גליל does not count at all, because rulings must come from near the שכינה.

steps.title: Leap years and new months are declared only by day
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that עיבור השנה and קידוש החודש must be done in the daytime. If done at night, they do not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The בית דין makes a leap year only during the day. If they did it at night, it is not a leap year. The בית דין sets the new month only during the day. If they did it at night, the month is not set.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with a time rule: declaring a leap year and setting the new month must happen during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two parallel rules, one for the year and one for the month. Each has an 'after the fact' clause: doing it at night does not count at all. Compare step 11, where a leap year declared in the גליל did count after the fact. Here, nighttime is a deeper problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Making the year a leap year by adding a month.
The בית דין officially declaring that a new month has begun.
It is not a leap year. The act simply does not count.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה אֶלָּא בְּיוֹם,
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: We do not make the year a leap year except during the day,
and if they made it a leap year at night, it is not a leap year.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ אֶלָּא בַּיּוֹם,
phrases.english: And we do not set the new month except during the day,
and if they set it at night, it is not set.
phrases.notes: 'Set' here means the בית דין officially announcing that the new month has started.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה אֶלָּא בְּיוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The earlier steps covered where a leap year is declared. This step adds a rule about when: only by day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עיבור השנה and קידוש החודש are valid only in the daytime. Done at night, they are invalid even after the fact.
steps.whyThisMatters: This time rule treats setting the calendar like a court action, which the next steps prove from a פסוק.

steps.title: רב אבא asks for the source
steps.stepSummary: רב אבא asks which פסוק teaches that the month is set only by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אבא said: What is the פסוק that teaches this?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אבא asks which פסוק is the source for the daytime rule. This is a setup line: he answers it himself right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave the rule without a reason. רב אבא wants to root it in a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is the verse?' A request for the source in תנ"ך.

phrases.english: Rav Abba said: What is the verse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural source of the ברייתא in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that קידוש החודש must happen by day?

steps.title: The פסוק about the שופר is about ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אבא quotes 'תקעו בחדש שופר בכסה ליום חגנו' and shows it speaks about ראש השנה, the חג when the moon is hidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Blow the שופר at the new month, at the hidden time, for the day of our חג.' Which חג comes when the moon is hidden? It must be ראש השנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אבא begins his answer. First he shows that the פסוק is talking about ראש השנה, a day set by the start of the month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בַּכֵּסֶה means 'covered' or 'hidden'. Only ראש השנה falls on the first day of a month, when the new moon can barely be seen. So the פסוק is about a חג that depends on setting the new month. This links the פסוק to קידוש החודש and prepares the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Blow the שופר at the new month' (תהלים 81:4).
At the hidden or covered time, when the moon cannot be seen.
'You must say.' This means there is only one possible answer.
The only חג on the first of the month.

phrases.english: 'Blow the shofar at the new month,
at the hidden time, for the day of our festival.'
Which festival is it on which the moon is hidden?
phrases.notes: The word for 'month' here really means the moon, which is still too thin to see on the first of the month.

phrases.english: You must say: this is Rosh HaShana.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּקְעוּ בַחֹדֶשׁ שׁוֹפָר בַּכֵּסֶה לְיוֹם חַגֵּנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of step 16 by identifying what the פסוק is about.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק speaks about ראש השנה, a day set by the new month. This sets up the link to the next פסוק.

steps.title: The month is set by day, just like a court judgment
steps.stepSummary: The next פסוק calls this a משפט (judgment). Court judgments happen by day, so קידוש החודש must also happen by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the next פסוק says: 'For it is a law for ישראל, a judgment of the God of יעקב.' Just as a court judgment is done by day, so too setting the month is done by day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אבא finishes his proof. The פסוק calls setting the day of ראש השנה a 'judgment', so it must follow the rule of judgments and be done in the daytime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof uses a comparison: מה... אף (just as... so too). Court cases are judged by day, and setting the month is called a משפט, so it must also be done by day. The פסוק is about ראש השנה, but the conclusion covers קידוש החודש in general, since ראש השנה is simply one new month.

keyTerms.meaning: A law or decree.
A judgment, like a ruling in court.
'Just as... so too...' A comparison that carries a rule from one case to another.

steps.whatToRemember: קידוש החודש counts as a משפט, a court ruling. Like every court ruling, it must be done by day. At night it does not count.
steps.whyThisMatters: Calling קידוש החודש a משפט explains why doing it at night is not just less good but invalid. A court ruling given at night is not a real ruling.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'For it is a statute for Israel,'
'a judgment of the God of Jacob.'
Just as judgment is by day,
so too the setting of the month is by day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְתִיב: כִּי חֹק לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִשְׁפָּט לֵאלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof that step 17 began, by linking ראש השנה to the word משפט.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Setting the month is called a משפט, and משפט is done only by day. So קידוש החודש must be by day.

steps.title: A new teaching about leap years begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens another ברייתא about when the בית דין does not make a leap year. Its details continue in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The בית דין does not make the year a leap year...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא starts a new ברייתא listing cases when a leap year is not declared, and the rest of it comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening words appear here, so no full rule has been given yet. It continues the theme of rules for declaring a leap year, which the coming text will spell out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We do not make a leap year.' This introduces cases when it is not done.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: We do not make the year a leap year…

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the daytime rule, the גמרא opens a new ברייתא on the same subject of leap years.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening of a ברייתא listing conditions under which a leap year is not declared. The details continue in the next section.
